1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R Is Now an 833-Piece Mattel Brick Shop Set That Can Be Customized
14 photos
Photo: Mattel
Slowly but surely, Mattel’s newest side business, the so-called Brick Shop, continues to grow with the addition of new cars that can be built at scale, in as-accurate-as-possible form. After the two Hondas announced at the beginning of the year, the Civic EF and S2000, it’s now time for another major Japanese nameplate to do the same.
Taking advantage of the 2026 Paris Motor Show that opened its doors this week, the toy maker announced the launch of a replica of the 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R, or, as it’s known in some circles, the Hakosuka.
Trying to stay as close as possible to the vehicle that’s considered by many the reason why the GT-R grew to become the icon that it is today, Mattel worked on the project with its Hot Wheels brand to create a 1:16 scale replica.
The miniature Nissan comes together after no less than 833 pieces of interlocking plastic bricks are properly put together and, when complete, appears decorated with the classic white racing livery with printed red stripes.
There are some functional elements included in the design, including a functional steering wheel and an opening hood that lifts out of the way to reveal a replica of the Nissan’s engine, a piece of hardware that comes with detailing, but no working parts.
The very interesting thing about this design, the result of the first-ever collaboration between Mattel and Nissan, is that it has been created with customization in mind. More specifically, fans can choose to install a custom decal sheet, one of two wheel cover sets (one of them made in metal), and a bunch of extra parts, including a front splitter, headlight covers, and an intercooler.
Officially titled the Mattel Brick Shop x Hot Wheels 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R , the set will become available in stores in January 2027, and it will sell for $59.99 to anyone over the age of ten. For that, the toy maker also throws in a metal signature plate and an exclusive, matching, 1:64 scale Hot Wheels die-cast toy.
Aside from the Nissan performance car announced today, Mattel already offers through the Brick Shop models from a large number of carmakers, including, in no particular order, Audi, Lamborghini, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz, Acura, Chevrolet, Honda, Cadillac, Aston Martin, and Toyota.
As for what models can be had in this form, you can think about the likes of the Cadillac Project GTP Hypercar, Maserati MC20, 1968 Chevrolet Camaro, Mercedes-Benz 300 SL, Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport, and 1990 Acura NSX.
All of these vehicles, no matter the series they’re part of, come as exact scale replicas of the real-world cars and trucks. Unlike competitor LEGO, which generally steers clear of using metal parts, Mattel’s sets do include them wherever and whenever possible.
